title: [Android] CameraX preview is rotated 90 degrees
body: After upgrading to camera 0.11.0+2, which resolves to camera_android_camerax 0.6.8+3, the Android camera preview on my Pixel 1 is rotated by 90 degrees. The same preview worked with camera_android_camerax 0.6.7+2. I am using CameraPreview and expect it to display in the correct orientation without manual rotation.

symptoms_visible: On my Pixel 1, CameraPreview is rotated by 90 degrees with camera 0.11.0+2 and camera_android_camerax 0.6.8+3.
N0.label: N0 rotated CameraX preview reported

symptoms_visible: The preview is still rotated on versions after camera_android_camerax 0.6.7+2, both with the regular Skia renderer and when I enable Impeller.
N1_x.label: N1_x duplicate-resolution aftermath

symptoms_visible: The preview remains rotated on my Pixel 1, while the same code displays correctly on an old participant10 device running Android 5.1.1.
N2.label: N2 device-specific contrast collected

symptoms_visible: I can reproduce the incorrect live preview on the Pixel 1 API 29 emulator exactly as on the physical device.
Across the affected devices, the live preview can be sideways, inverted, or stretched depending on the device orientation, while a captured photo can display normally afterward.
N3.label: N3 cross-device orientation matrix established

symptoms_visible: With camera_android_camerax 0.6.9, the preview is correctly oriented on affected API 29 phones in the usual startup case.
If the app starts while the device is already in landscape, or on some naturally landscape devices, the preview can still be rotated or inverted.
N4.label: N4 API 29 correction partially verified

symptoms_visible: Wrapping CameraPreview in a RotatedBox can make the initial portrait view look correct, but the preview becomes incorrectly oriented when I rotate the device or use the opposite landscape orientation.
N4_manual_x.label: N4_manual_x fixed quarter-turn workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: With the release that removed the earlier preview-rotation logic, the preview is still rotated on affected participant10 devices and tablets, and a physical Pixel 7 that previously displayed correctly becomes rotated by 90 degrees.
N5_x.label: N5_x rotation-removal fix aftermath

symptoms_visible: After updating to camera_android_camerax 0.6.14, the camera preview is correctly oriented on the affected participant10 tablet and on the customer's physical device.
N6.label: N6 final package verified on physical devices

symptoms_visible: The live CameraX preview stays correctly oriented as the physical device orientation changes after updating to camera_android_camerax 0.6.14.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

symptoms_visible: The preview remains rotated on my Pixel 1, while the same code displays correctly on an old participant10 device running Android 5.1.1.
N2b.label: N2b canonical merge (no blind-branch knowledge)

solution.intent: Treat the report as a duplicate of the earlier Impeller preview-rotation issue and ask the reporter to retry on the latest Flutter main branch containing that fix.
solution.concrete_example: This looks like issue 149294, which is fixed on main; switch to the latest main channel and rerun the sample.

edges.comment: The issue was initially closed as a duplicate. The reporter rejected that resolution with version and renderer evidence: the regression appears after 0.6.7+2 and reproduces with both Skia and Impeller.

question_patterns: Can you test the same code on another Android device, preferably a non-Pixel device?
Does the preview rotate incorrectly on any other phone you have available?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked an old participant10 running Android 5.1.1, API 22, and everything worked as expected there. My options for testing more devices are currently limited.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It is rotated by the same 90 degrees on every Android device I tested, including the API 22 participant10.
The participant10 test is still correct, but it is running API 23 rather than API 22.

question_patterns: Does the rotation bug also happen with the Impeller renderer, or only with Skia?
Could you try running with --enable-impeller and tell me if the preview rotation changes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: This is produced after the fix while running the regular Skia engine — and I also tried running the app with Impeller: same wrong rotation.

edges.comment: The first comparison suggested a device or backend-dependent behavior rather than a universal CameraPreview layout error.

question_patterns: Which other devices and orientations reproduce the incorrect preview?
Can you test portrait, both landscape directions, and naturally landscape devices and describe the raw results?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Reproduced it more broadly: the Pixel 1 shows it consistently, the API 29 emulator reproduces it too, and it happens across orientations — device screenshots attached.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The live preview is correct in every orientation; only the saved video is rotated when played back.
The same orientation-dependent behavior occurs on a different participant10 model and a different Pixel Tablet API image.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce the physical Pixel 1 behavior in an emulator using its last supported Android API?
Does a Pixel 1 API 29 emulator show the same preview orientation?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I configured a Pixel 1 emulator with the API 29 system image, and it behaves exactly like my real Pixel 1: the preview is always incorrect.

question_patterns: Is the captured image itself rotated or stretched, or only the live CameraPreview?
How does the photo look when displayed separately after capture?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Before capture, the CameraX preview is rotated and stretched. After I take the photo and display it with photo_view, that image is not stretched.

edges.comment: Reports from multiple affected users are folded into one simulated user side. The evidence distinguishes this live-preview bug from the separately tracked rotated recorded-video playback issue.

question_patterns: Can you override camera_android_camerax to 0.6.9 and retest the affected API 29 preview?
Please test the package containing the API 29 boundary correction and report only what happens to the live preview.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the override. On the affected Android 10/API 29 phone, camera_android_camerax 0.6.9 makes the live preview orientation correct.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The preview remains rotated by exactly the same amount on API 29 with camera_android_camerax 0.6.9.

question_patterns: With that package, what happens if the app starts while the device is already in landscape?
Please test all four orientations, with auto-rotate on and off, and report whether every preview is correct.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Starting the camera while the phone is held in landscape gives a wrongly rotated preview — sometimes it comes up sideways, sometimes upside down, depending on which way I'm holding it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: All four orientations remain correct, including when the app starts in landscape and on naturally landscape tablets.
Landscape left and right are both wrong, but the exact direction of the rotation is reversed on my device.

edges.comment: Testing 0.6.9 is a handler-requested package/version probe, so it is a clarification rather than a solution edge. It corrected the main API 29 case but exposed remaining orientation-change and landscape-start behavior.

solution.intent: Remove the plugin's previously added preview-rotation correction and rely on the underlying surface/backend to orient the preview automatically.
solution.concrete_example: Use the package produced by PR 8256, which removes the earlier CameraX preview-rotation logic and returns the preview without that correction.

edges.comment: The removal was tested and later released, but affected participant10 devices and tablets remained wrong, and previously correct devices such as a physical Pixel 7 became rotated. It was therefore not the complete fix.

solution.intent: Manually wrap CameraPreview in a fixed RotatedBox and AspectRatio to compensate for the visible 90-degree error.
solution.concrete_example: Wrap CameraPreview in RotatedBox(quarterTurns: 1) and use cameraController.value.aspectRatio for the child AspectRatio.

edges.comment: A fixed quarter-turn made some initial portrait screenshots look correct, but users retracted it as a general solution because it fails when orientation changes or the opposite landscape direction is used.

question_patterns: Can you update to camera_android_camerax 0.6.14 and verify the preview on the same affected physical device?
Please update, test the package containing PR 8629, and report whether the preview remains correctly oriented.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I updated to camera_android_camerax 0.6.14 — the preview orientation is correct now on my devices.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The preview is still rotated on both physical devices with 0.6.14 after removing the workaround.
It works on the same affected devices with 0.6.14, but I tested a rear camera instead of the front camera first.

edges.comment: Post-release verification from affected physical-device users is folded into one simulated user. A separate naturally landscape industrial-display case was identified for follow-up rather than treated as evidence that the main fix failed.

solution.intent: Use camera_android_camerax 0.6.14 or later, whose preview widget responds to orientation-stream updates and applies a rotation correction only when SurfaceProducer reports that it does not handle crop and rotation.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade to camera_android_camerax 0.6.14. PR 8629 rebuilds the preview when device orientation changes and uses SurfaceProducer.handlesCropAndRotation() instead of an Android API-level guess to decide whether Flutter must rotate the preview.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied version boundaries, device/orientation matrices, and package-test outcomes. Engineers derived the mechanism: orientation calculations were updating through a stream without rebuilding the Texture-based preview, and Android API level was only an unreliable approximation of whether the active SurfaceProducer backend already handled crop and rotation.

edges.comment: Final resolution from PR 8629, published in camera_android_camerax 0.6.14 and confirmed on affected physical devices. Emulator-specific behavior and naturally landscape industrial hardware were treated as separate follow-up cases.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify both parts of the root cause: orientation-stream changes did not rebuild the preview widget, and Android API level was an unreliable proxy for whether the SurfaceProducer backend already handled crop and rotation.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the regression after camera_android_camerax 0.6.7+2, different results across devices and orientations, the partial API 29 improvement, and physical-device verification of 0.6.14.

The final fix must use a preview that rebuilds on orientation changes and SurfaceProducer.handlesCropAndRotation() to decide whether an additional correction is needed; recommend camera_android_camerax 0.6.14 or later.

Must not close the report as a duplicate of the earlier Impeller-only issue, rely solely on renderer selection or Android API level, remove all correction unconditionally, or present a fixed RotatedBox quarter-turn as the general fix.
Must distinguish the live CameraPreview rotation defect from rotated saved-video playback, which was tracked separately.
Must require verification on an affected physical device without a manual rotation workaround before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Flutter developer who can inspect plugin implementations, compare transitive package versions, switch renderers, run emulators with specific API images, and test dependency overrides; additional affected developers with varied hardware are folded into the same simulated user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical, evidence-driven, and cooperative. Provides precise package versions and orientation steps, challenges premature conclusions politely, and reports raw device-test outcomes without claiming the underlying engine mechanism.
